name: Shianbashi and Doza
tagline: The entertainment district, with Chinatown next door
description: Nagasaki's nightlife quarter in the flat centre of the city, a grid of izakaya, small bars and restaurants running up against Shinchi Chinatown, one of only three in Japan. The trams pass along the main street and the harbour is a few minutes south.
bestFor: Stays that want the restaurants, Chinatown and the trams on the doorstep
pros: The city's bars and restaurants immediately there
Chinatown and its food a minute away
cons: Noise from the entertainment district at night
Flat and dense with little green

name: Minamiyamate and Glover Garden
tagline: The old foreign settlement on the southern slope
description: The hillside above the harbour where the nineteenth century foreign merchants built their houses, now the Glover Garden, with Oura church, the old consulates and stone-paved lanes climbing between them. The views over the harbour are the best in the city and the streets are the most attractive.
bestFor: Stays that want the harbour view and the city's foreign-settlement history
pros: The best harbour views in Nagasaki
Glover Garden and Oura church on the doorstep
cons: Steep, with stairs rather than streets in places
Day visitors around the main sites
Few shops and no supermarket close by

name: Urakami and the Peace Park
tagline: North of the centre, around the hypocentre and the cathedral
description: The northern valley where the bomb detonated in 1945, now holding the Peace Park, the atomic bomb museum and the rebuilt Urakami cathedral, with the university hospital and a large residential population around them. It is flatter than most of Nagasaki, well served by trams and cheaper than the centre.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting flat ground, trams and rents below the centre
pros: Flat streets, which is rare in Nagasaki
Direct tram to the centre in fifteen minutes
cons: The area's history is heavy and unavoidable
Visitor traffic around the Peace Park

name: Inasa and the Western Slope
tagline: Below the ropeway, facing the city across the harbour
description: The residential slope on the western side of the harbour beneath Mount Inasa, whose summit gives the night view Nagasaki is known for, reached by a ropeway from the foot of the hill. Housing is stepped up the hillside with wide views back across the water to the city.
bestFor: Stays that want the famous night view as the daily outlook
pros: The Mount Inasa ropeway and its view immediately there
Wide outlook over the harbour and the city
Quieter and cheaper than the east bank
cons: Steep slopes and long stair climbs
Fifteen to twenty minutes into the centre

name: Dejima and the Waterfront
tagline: The reconstructed Dutch island and the harbour front
description: The harbourside strip around the restored Dejima, the artificial island that was Japan's only permitted contact with Europe for two centuries, now rebuilt as a museum quarter. Newer apartment buildings, the ferry terminal and the seaside park run along the water beside it.
bestFor: People who want newer flats, the harbour walk and the ferries
pros: Dejima and the harbour park on the doorstep
Ferries to the islands and the tram both close
cons: Less character than the hillside quarters
Exposed to wind off the harbour
